name: Stand With Crypto
mission: Organizes people who own and build with crypto to push for clear, common-sense crypto rules in the US.
about: Stand With Crypto helps advocates contact their representatives, register to vote and see where candidates stand on crypto. As a 501(c)(4) social welfare organization it can lobby without limits, which is also why gifts to it are not tax-deductible.

name: St. Jude Children's Research Hospital
legalName: St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, Inc.
mission: Finds cures for childhood cancer and other life-threatening diseases, and saves children through research and treatment.
about: Families never receive a bill from St. Jude for treatment, travel, housing or food. Danny Thomas founded it in Memphis in 1962, and it shares its discoveries freely with doctors around the world.

name: American Red Cross
mission: Prevents and alleviates human suffering in the face of emergencies.
about: The Red Cross shelters, feeds and supports people after disasters, supplies about 40% of the blood used in US hospitals, and trains millions in first aid and CPR. Clara Barton founded it in 1881.

name: Doctors Without Borders
address: 40 Rector St, 16th Fl, New York, NY 10006
mission: Delivers emergency medical care to people caught in conflict, epidemics, disasters and exclusion from health care.
about: Doctors Without Borders (Médecins Sans Frontières) runs medical projects in more than 70 countries and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1999. It decides where to work based on need alone.

name: UNICEF USA
mission: Supports UNICEF's work to save and protect the world's most vulnerable children.
about: UNICEF works in more than 190 countries and territories on vaccines, clean water, nutrition, education and emergency relief for children. UNICEF USA raises support for that work in the US.

name: Feeding America
address: 161 N Clark St, Ste 700, Chicago, IL 60601
mission: Works to end hunger in America through a nationwide network of food banks.
about: Feeding America's network of more than 200 food banks and tens of thousands of pantries and meal programs gets food to people in every county in the US.

name: Habitat for Humanity
address: 285 Peachtree Center Ave NE, Ste 270, Atlanta, GA 30303
mission: Brings people together to build homes, communities and hope.
about: Habitat partners with families to build and repair homes they buy with affordable mortgages, working alongside volunteers in all 50 states and more than 70 countries.

name: World Wildlife Fund
mission: Conserves nature and reduces the most pressing threats to the diversity of life on Earth.
about: WWF protects wildlife and the places they live, from forests and oceans to freshwater, and works with communities and companies on climate and food.

name: charity: water
mission: Brings clean and safe drinking water to people in developing countries.
about: charity: water funds wells, rainwater catchments and filtration systems with local partners. Private supporters cover its operating costs, so public donations go straight to water projects.

name: GiveDirectly
mission: Sends cash directly to people living in extreme poverty, to spend on what they need most.
about: GiveDirectly delivers cash transfers by mobile money, mostly in East Africa, and publishes research on what happens when people living in poverty get to choose.

name: Wikimedia Foundation
address: 1 Sansome St, Ste 1895, San Francisco, CA 94104
mission: Hosts Wikipedia and its sister projects, so everyone can share in the sum of all knowledge.
about: The Wikimedia Foundation runs the servers, software and legal defense behind Wikipedia, which volunteers write in more than 300 languages, free and without ads.

name: Electronic Frontier Foundation
mission: Defends civil liberties in the digital world: privacy, free expression and innovation.
about: EFF fights in court and in Congress for users' rights online. It won the case that established computer code as protected speech, which matters to everyone who writes open-source software.

name: Coin Center
address: 650 Massachusetts Ave NW, Fl 6, Washington, DC 20001
mission: Researches and advocates for policy that protects the freedom to build and use open crypto networks.
about: Coin Center is the leading independent policy center for crypto in Washington. Tax-deductible gifts go to its 501(c)(3), CC Foundation; its advocacy arm, Coin Center Inc, is a separate 501(c)(4).

name: Make-A-Wish
address: 1702 E Highland Ave, Ste 400, Phoenix, AZ 85016
mission: Creates life-changing wishes for children with critical illnesses.
about: Make-A-Wish has granted wishes to hundreds of thousands of children in the US since a boy named Chris became an honorary police officer in Phoenix in 1980.

name: Save the Children
address: 500 Kings Hwy E, Ste 400, Fairfield, CT 06825
mission: Gives children a healthy start in life, the opportunity to learn and protection from harm.
about: Save the Children works in the US and around the world on child health, education and emergency response, and speaks up for children's rights.

name: American Cancer Society
address: 270 Peachtree St NW, Ste 1300, Atlanta, GA 30303
mission: Improves the lives of people with cancer and their families through advocacy, research and patient support.
about: The American Cancer Society funds cancer research, runs a 24/7 helpline, and gives patients free rides to treatment and free places to stay near hospitals.

name: ASPCA
legalName: The American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals
mission: Provides effective means for the prevention of cruelty to animals throughout the United States.
about: The ASPCA rescues animals from abuse, runs animal hospitals and a poison control center, and helps shelters across the country get pets adopted.

name: Khan Academy
mission: Provides a free, world-class education for anyone, anywhere.
about: Khan Academy offers free lessons and practice in math, science, reading and more, used by students and teachers in nearly every country.

name: Food for Lane County
mission: Reduces hunger by creating access to food in Lane County, Oregon.
about: Eugene's food bank collects and distributes food through pantries, meal sites and programs across Lane County, home of the University of Oregon.

name: Wounded Warrior Project
mission: Connects, serves and empowers wounded veterans, service members and their families.
about: Wounded Warrior Project offers mental health support, physical health and wellness programs, career help and benefits advice to veterans injured on or after 9/11, at no cost to them.
